alisa: Heads-up — CI perf regression after merge (PR #4129) that inserted quantization routing. Canary 95pct latency up ~35% on int8 bench, blocking rollout :exclamation:

ci-bot: CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/12345 — perf-suite/int8 exceeded threshold (95th 74ms -> 100ms)

devin: Ugh. Is this the new quant-insertion pass that landed yesterday?

alisa: yeah, that one. my quick profile shows an extra memcpy and a fallback to scalar dequant for tails. Attaching small profile snippet: ```
hot functions:
  DequantKernel::apply 42%
  KernelSelector::score 18%
  KVCache::lookup 9%
  BatchCoalescer::emit 7%
  memcpy 6%
```

maria: @devin can you run the bisect loop? If this is from that merge we should identify the offending commit fast.

devin: starting bisect across last 10 commits. command: `git bisect start --term-good=good --term-bad=bad` then build/invoke perf harness: `./tools/ci/run_perf.sh --suite=int8 --runs=10`

perf-bot: Note: perf variance is ~2-3% normally. 35% is well outside noise. TL;DR: investigate kernel selector changes and dequant fastpaths.

jordan: I noticed the new pass rewrites graph ops to insert a "quant-insert" op and then relies on kernel selector to pick fused vs unfused kernels. Might be a selector priority bug.

devin: bisect result: bad at commit a7f3c2f (PR 4129, quant-insertion). Good at prior commit e9b2a01.

alisa: thanks. Can someone dump the selector decision log for a typical request? `REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1` yields per-layer choice. snippet: ```
layer 12: selected kernel fused_int8_dequant_ffn (lat 1.8ms)
layer 13: selected kernel scalar_dequant_ffn (lat 9.1ms)  <-- suspicious
layer 14: selected kernel fused_int8_dequant_ffn (lat 1.7ms)
```

maria: scalar choice on layer 13 is the issue. Why did selector pick scalar? inputs: tail_len=11, seq=128, model=redwood-7b-int8, hw=rtx-a6000.

jordan: the selector has a new rule that penalizes fused kernels when tail_len < 16 because of alignment assumptions. That rule was added in the quant-insertion change to avoid misaligned vector loads, but it didn't add a memmove fastpath.

alisa: So we now do scalar dequant for tails -> big perf hit. Possible fixes:
- add memmove/fallback fastpath before scalar dequant (cheap),
- relax the selector penalty and let fused kernel handle misaligned tails (risky),
- do a short prefix KVCACHE normalization to pad tails to 16 (affects memory).

devin: Quick patch candidate: in KernelSelector, only penalize fused kernels if `seq % 16 != 0 && tail_len > 32`. That keeps fused for small tails. I'll prototype and run perf.

maria: Also we should add a microbenchmark for tail cases to CI so this doesn't regress silently.

devin: patched locally, ran perf harness: 95th moved back to baseline within noise (74ms -> 76ms). Patch diff: ```diff
- if (tail_len < 16) score -= 50;
+ if (tail_len < 16 && tail_len > 32) score -= 50;
```

jordan: typo? condition looks impossible (tail_len <16 && >32). maybe you mean `tail_len >= 16 || tail_len <= 32`?

devin: oof, brainfart in chat. Actual patch: `if (tail_len > 32) score -= 50;` I've pushed branch `fix/selector-tail-fastpath` -> PR 4182.

ci-bot: PR 4182 opened: https://git.redwood/PR/4182 — runs: unit, integration, perf (tail-microbench included)

perf-bot: Perf run for PR 4182: int8-canary: 95th 75ms (baseline 74ms) — within acceptable delta.

alisa: Good. We should still add an explicit memmove fastpath in the runtime to avoid depending on selector heuristics. Follow-up ticket?

maria: Created ticket INF-1293: "Dequant tail fastpath + tail microbench in CI" and assigned to devex/eng-runtime.

jordan: rolling out PR 4182 to canary after green. We'll hold the full rollout until we have the fastpath or extra telemetry.

devin: merging canary patch now. `git merge --no-ff fix/selector-tail-fastpath`

ci-bot: Canary pipeline green. Deploying to canary cluster — rolling update start.

alisa: Monitoring dashboard: token-level latency and kernel-choice telemetry enabled. :eyes:

perf-bot: Early canary metrics: tail-heavy traffic shows 95th down from 102ms -> 76ms across 10 minutes. No errors.

maria: good catch team. Lessons: when adding quantization routing, include tail/misalignment microbench and a memmove fastpath before penalizing fused kernels.

jordan: Agreed. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and include the selector decision logs in release notes.

alisa: Marking rollout = blocked -> unblocked after PR 4182 merged to main. Will keep INF-1293 open until fastpath shipped. :white_check_mark:
